system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel — Buyer review

**Overall recommendation:** Do not accept the Seller’s package as drafted. The principal buyer risks are the broad liability and disclosure exclusions, completion without resolved Bluefen and Riverlark requirements, and the allocation of identified liabilities under a debt-free/cash-free deal. The points below are negotiation recommendations; the complete SPA and underlying DD documents should be checked before finalising drafting.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price: AUD 4.8m**. | A higher general warranty cap, negotiated alongside insurance and recovery security; separate treatment for fundamental warranties and specific indemnities. | **Negotiate upward.** A 20% cap may leave the Buyer carrying a substantial loss; do not let it operate as a global cap for all claim categories. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; aggregate qualifying claims must exceed **AUD 250,000**, with only the excess recoverable. | A lower de minimis and a **tipping basket**, so the full qualifying amount is recoverable once the basket is exceeded; related claims aggregated. | **Negotiate.** The proposed deductible basket shifts the first AUD 250,000 of qualifying loss to the Buyer, in addition to excluding small claims. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General warranty notice period of **18 months after Completion**; limitations apply to all claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with longer, separately specified periods for tax and other relevant categories. | **Extend and segregate.** Eighteen months may expire before issues emerge through two audit or reporting cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limit. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, authority, ownership, shares and encumbrances; cap at least the **full purchase price**, with a materially longer survival period. | **Reject equal treatment.** Defects in the Seller’s ability to sell or the Buyer’s ownership of the shares go to the essence of the transaction. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to claims of any nature. | Express carve-out for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation, including from caps, thresholds, time limits, disclosure, knowledge, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions. | **Insist on an effective, overriding carve-out.** The Seller’s all-claims wording could otherwise impair remedies for fraudulent conduct; check attribution and interaction with the rest of the SPA. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the whole data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records. | Disclosure only against identified warranties and only where **fairly disclosed** with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; a fixed, identifiable disclosure bundle. | **Reject blanket disclosure.** Mere inclusion in a large body of material should not automatically qualify every warranty. Preserve specific remedies for known issues. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | No constructive or imputed knowledge bar; ideally no knowledge qualifier beyond fair disclosure, with no effect on specific indemnities or fraud claims. | **Delete or narrow substantially.** “Discoverable” shifts diligence risk to the Buyer even where a matter was not identified or fairly explained. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. No final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions is disclosed. | A completion condition requiring valid written consent **and satisfaction or waiver of its conditions** on terms acceptable to Buyer; stronger Seller obligations to procure it. | **Do not complete on consent alone.** DD-002 identifies conditions in clause 11.3 and approximately AUD 3.6m in FY26 revenue; obtain and review the consent and evidence of compliance. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release to follow Completion. | Repayment at or before Completion from Seller proceeds, verified payout figure and binding discharge/release arrangements effective at Completion, with registration follow-up. | **Make repayment and release completion deliverables.** A post-completion release leaves debt and security risk with the Buyer, contrary to debt-free/cash-free economics. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses are not separately shown in the funds flow; Seller says they are its matter. | Express Seller funding or a purchase-price/debt-like adjustment for bonuses that become payable and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, without double counting. | **Resolve and itemise before signing.** Completion and continued-employment conditions, payment timing and on-costs must be checked so the Company does not bear an unpriced Seller cost. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; DD-010 records **AUD 180,000 open**, without independent proof of non-payment. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is disclosed. | Verify payment; obtain receipt and effective assignment or confirmation of title. Expand the indemnity to resulting IP ownership, licence, infringement and remediation losses, costs and claims. | **Broaden protection and cure title.** Payment status is unverified, and a payment-only indemnity may not cover the consequences of a failure to transfer Project Materials. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter said not to be expected to be material; access, scope, notification and loss remain unresolved. | Complete a prompt investigation; preserve evidence; assess notification and remediation obligations; obtain a tailored indemnity for pre-completion incident losses and response costs, with appropriate conduct rights. | **Treat as an open risk, not a confirmed breach.** The unintended link and potentially affected records warrant investigation and contractual protection despite uncertainty about access or loss. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** described as ordinary-course costs. | Review DD-008 and DD-011 together; establish timing, scope, termination rights, accrual and whether each is avoidable, then allocate any pre-completion or non-ordinary-course cost through the price mechanics or specific protection. | **Do not accept the classification without evidence.** The disclosure does not establish that all three costs are ordinary-course, unavoidable or properly allocated. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations apply to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise; broad exclusive-remedy language. | Distinct, expressly drafted regimes for general and fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, price adjustments, completion obligations and fraud, with clear precedence and no unintended overlaps. | **Redraft the architecture.** Otherwise general caps, thresholds or deadlines may defeat separately negotiated protections and debt-free/cash-free adjustments. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Harbourglass as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Independently verify issued capital, ownership and encumbrances against the register, constitutional and corporate records and relevant searches; obtain transfers, approvals, releases and updated register at Completion. | **Verify and obtain fundamental warranties.** The register is relevant evidence, but the disclosure does not establish that the Buyer has verified title or that shares are unencumbered. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties considered settled under the general regime. | Reopen tax protections: dedicated tax covenant/indemnity for pre-completion liabilities, appropriate survival and exclusions. Reopen IP warranties covering ownership, licences, infringement and key developed IP, alongside the Ironquay protection. | **Keep open pending diligence and drafting.** General warranty limits may be inadequate for liabilities discovered later or for material IP defects. |

**Other diligence points:** DD-007 identifies a **lease notification**, not an established landlord-consent requirement. DD-009 identifies an **assignment restriction**, not an established consent requirement merely on a share sale. Check the documents and transaction structure before requiring either consent.
=== END ADVICE ===
